text:
ashley: FYI, customer acme-prod reporting a production failure - tool/function call to `invoice_lookup` is returning 422 schema errors since ~09:12 UTC. They say it started after a spike in traffic. Full customer logs pasted below. :grimacing:

ashley: customer stacktrace snippet:```
2026-03-05T09:11:58Z ERROR tool-router: invoke failed status=422 route=/tools/invoice_lookup payload={"invoice_id": ["inv_123"]} error=SchemaValidationError: invoice_id expected string but got array
````

sophia: copying their request body they used in prod:```json
{
  "tool": "invoice_lookup",
  "args": {"invoice_id": ["inv_123"]},
  "model": "redwood-llm-1"
}
```

devon: :eyes: That matches our validator - invoice_lookup expects a single string id. Wondering how a list got through. Any gateway or client transformation?

maya: Noting that our router has a permissive deserializer for `args` when content-type is application/json; we validate schema later in the tool shim. Could be a client SDK bug that serializes single-value fields as arrays for retry logic.

ashley: Customer says they send via our JS SDK v1.3.2. They included repro curl that fails:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_prod_xxx' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"tool":"invoice_lookup","args":{"invoice_id":["inv_123"]}}'
```

devon: Repro locally with that payload - got same 422. Minimal reproduction:```json
{ "tool":"invoice_lookup", "args": {"invoice_id": ["inv_abc"]}}```

maya: Two action items: (1) add stricter pre-validate in routing layer to coerce single-element arrays to scalars for legacy SDKs, (2) patch SDK docs and contact customer for immediate workaround.

ashley: Customer asks for mitigation now — can we add a temporary router-level fallback that coerces invoice_id arrays of length 1 into string?

devon: I can push a tiny hotfix to the router to detect schema mismatch on tool invocation and attempt single-element array -> scalar coercion. Deploy window ~5-10m if no regressions.

deploy-bot: Release plan created: redwood/router#542 - hotfix/allow-array-coercion. CI tests 18/19 passing, will run canary in us-west-2.

maya: Also recommend logging a distinct metric for "toolcall.coercion_applied" so we can measure how many requests rely on this fallback — we shouldn't mask real client bugs forever.

ashley: Sent customer the workaround (wrap invoice_id as string) and told them we are deploying a hotfix in ~10m. They asked about credits for failed requests — should we loop in billing?

devon: I'll patch and monitor. If canary is stable I'll promote. For billing, support should file a credit request after we quantify failed calls in last hour.

ashley: Understood. I'll capture counts once metric lands.

maya: Follow-up: after deployment we should update SDK changelog and ship a minor SDK patch that normalizes single-element arrays to string for known tool params to be defensive.

sophia: Customer replied: "Thanks, appreciate the quick response — workaround applied and will monitor. Please keep us posted." :thumbsup:

devon: Hotfix deployed to canary at 09:23 UTC. Initial telemetry: 42 coerced calls in canary region, 0 errors post-coercion. Rolling to 50% now.

deploy-bot: Canary -> prod rollout scheduled: progressing. No blocking alerts detected.

devon: Promotion complete at 09:31 UTC. No increase in error rate. Marking incident mitigated.

maya: Filed follow PRs: redwood/router#543 (metric + audit logs), redwood/sdk-js#210 (defensive normalization).

ashley: I'll follow up with customer about credits once we have exact failed count. Closing thread when billing confirms. Thanks team. :sparkles:
